MP is the reference leader for government-backed rare-earth magnet capacity: high evidence quality but high attention and above the preferred small/mid-cap hunting zone.
LEU fits the node through DOE-backed HALEU production; the critical later question is whether demonstration-scale support converts to commercial-scale capacity and durable revenue.
IPX is a speculative shadow candidate for domestic titanium capacity expansion; require market-cap verification, cash runway analysis, task-order follow-through, and production scale validation.
Future passes should screen DLA, DPA Title III, IBAS, DOE LPO, EXIM, and DoD Office of Strategic Capital records for additional public recipients where award size is material relative to revenue.

UAMY is the cleanest Layer 1B underfollowed candidate for government-backed capacity expansion because provided evidence describes both a DLA sole-source IDIQ and DPA grant tied to an obscure defense-critical material.
MP should be retained as a reference benchmark for rare-earth and magnet policy exposure, but not allowed to crowd out smaller suppliers in later discovery passes.

The highest-signal version of this node is not simply a press release announcing funding; it is a combination of scarce qualified supply, statutory sourcing pressure, funded purchase orders or offtakes, and contract value material relative to revenue.
Centrus Energy and BWX Technologies require direct evidence collection from DOE, DOD, NRC, company filings, and federal award databases before they can be upgraded from hypothesis candidates.

UAMY should remain in the speculative/underfollowed lane because the DLA IDIQ plus DPA award is unusually material relative to company scale, but future inclusion depends on delivery-order conversion, margin, and dilution checks.

LEU is a high-relevance mid-cap government-backed capacity name tied to DOE HALEU production; next layers should distinguish funded production revenue from non-finalized or subject-to-appropriations awards.

For government-backed capacity expansion, the highest-quality signals are funded delivery orders, exercised options, finalized task orders, cost-share disbursements, and offtake/price-floor mechanics rather than announced ceiling values.

The next search pass should map subtier public suppliers beneath BWXT, MP Materials, and UAMY, especially testing/certification, specialty metals, regulated components, feedstock logistics, and qualification bottlenecks.

UAMY is a high-priority Layer 2 verification candidate for government-backed capacity expansion because the DLA IDIQ appears large relative to historical revenue, but survival depends on delivery orders, margin, feedstock, and dilution checks.

AREC/ReElement is a speculative micro-cap exception: the government-backed financing headline is large, but AREC shareholder economics require ownership, consolidation, warrant, and spin-off verification.
NB fits the EXIM loan-guarantee watchlist but should remain speculative until potential financing becomes binding and project capex, equity, offtake, and timeline are updated.

Critical minerals and rare-earth magnet chains are the strongest current mapping for this node because policy risk is converting into direct loans, DPA/OSC support, IDIQs, and strategic stockpile procurement.

Next search pass should screen federal award databases and SEC 8-K/10-Q filings for additional small-cap suppliers with DLA, DPA Title III, EXIM, DOE, CHIPS, or OSC awards where award size exceeds 25% of annual revenue.
